title: Théorie des cycles algébriques : conjectures de Hodge, Tate, Lefschetz, Weil : notes manuscrites (s.d.), lettre (1965).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (Prop. 2.1, stated on p.57). X and Y are smooth projective connected varieties over an algebraically closed field k, of dimensions n and m. Z is a 1-cycle on X×Y, so Z is a correspondence of codimension n+m-1. Write B_X = Pic^0_{X/k} (reduced) and A_Y = Alb(Y). For a divisor D ≡_alg 0 on X, the transpose tZ(D) = pr_{2*}((D×Y)·Z) is a 0-cycle on Y of degree 0. The proposition asserts that there is a unique homomorphism of abelian varieties u: B_X → A_Y with u(cl(D)) = S_Y(tZ(D)), where S_Y is the Albanese summation map.

This page, statement. The same u is characterised cohomologically, with Z_ℓ coefficients and ℓ prime to the characteristic. The following square must commute:
- top: u^{(1)}: H^1(A_Y) → H^1(B_X), pullback by u;
- left: φ_Y^{(1)}: H^1(Y) ≅ H^1(A_Y) via the Albanese map. Grothendieck marks it 'isom mod torsion'; with Z_ℓ coefficients it is in fact an isomorphism, since H^1 kills the torsion of H_1;
- bottom: a(γ(ξ)): H^1(Y) → H^{2n-1}(X)(n-1), the action of the class ξ of Z in H^{2(n+m-1)}(X×Y)(n+m-1), i.e. pull back, cup with ξ, push forward to X. The degree count is 1 + 2(n+m-1) - 2m = 2n-1;
- right: ψ_X: H^{2n-1}(X)(n-1) → H^1(B_X). This is Poincaré duality H^{2n-1}(X)(n) ≅ H^1(X)^∨ ≅ T_ℓ Alb_X, combined with the Weil pairing T_ℓ Alb_X ≅ T_ℓ(Pic^0_X)^∨(1).
Finally, u depends only on the numerical equivalence class of Z.

Proof sketch on this page.
1. The composite ψ_X ∘ a(γ(ξ)) ∘ (φ_Y^{(1)})^{-1} is induced by algebraic correspondence classes (all three factors are), hence is independent of ℓ.
2. By Lemma 1.7 (a map H^1(A) → H^1(B) coming from an algebraic correspondence between abelian varieties is u^{(1)} for a homomorphism u: B → A), it equals u^{(1)} for some u: B_X → A_Y.
3. It remains to prove u(cl(D)) = S_Y(tZ(D)) whenever tZ(D) is defined. Uniqueness is immediate, since every class in Pic^0(X) has a representative D with tZ(D) defined (moving lemma).
4. The next page first constructs u directly. Take the Poincaré divisor Θ on X×B_X and form C = π_*((1_Y×Θ)·(Z×1_{B_X})) on Y×B_X. Applying Lemma 1.1 to C gives u: B_X = A_{B_X} → A_Y with S_Y(Z(Θ(b))) = u(b).

Purpose. Section 2 is titled 'algébricité de certains homomorphismes de V.A. à l'aide de cohomologie ℓ-adique'. The aim is to show that maps on H^1 / H^{2n-1} induced by algebraic correspondences come from homomorphisms of abelian varieties. This is the degree-1 part of the standard-conjecture programme: the H^1 'motive' is the Picard/Albanese variety, and the Lefschetz-type inverse on H^1 is algebraic.
errors: In the proof the composite is written ψ_X a(γ(ξ)) φ_X^{(1)}. By the diagram it should be ψ_X ∘ a(γ(ξ)) ∘ (φ_Y^{(1)})^{-1}; the subscript X is a slip, and the inverse is needed.
Notation clash: ξ denotes the cohomology class of Z in γ(ξ), but on the same page ξ also denotes an element of Pic^0(X).

Integrality gap. The left arrow is only claimed to be an isomorphism mod torsion, so the composite is a priori defined over Q_ℓ or up to torsion. Getting an honest u (not just an element of Hom⊗Q) requires the direct construction on the next page, which Grothendieck indeed supplies.

The claim that u depends only on the numerical class of Z is stated without proof here. It follows from the classical Weil trace argument: tr(u∘v) is an intersection number Z·T for divisorial correspondences T, and the trace pairing between Hom(B,A)_Q and Hom(A,B)_Q is nondegenerate. The argument is standard but not trivial.
The superscript on γ in the diagram is garbled (looks like m-n-1 with corrections). The correct codimension of Z is n+m-1.

ideas.what: Homomorphism Pic^0(X) → Alb(Y) induced by a 1-cycle correspondence Z on X×Y, D ↦ S_Y(tZ(D))
ideas.modern_name: action of correspondences on Picard/Albanese varieties
ideas.usually_credited_to: Weil (Variétés abéliennes et courbes algébriques), Matsusaka, Lang (Abelian Varieties, 1959)
ideas.where_published: Classical; Lang's book; used in Kleiman's 'Algebraic cycles and the Weil conjectures' (Dix exposés, 1968)

ideas.what: Compatibility of that homomorphism with the ℓ-adic action of the cycle class on H^1 → H^{2n-1}, via Albanese and Weil-pairing identifications
ideas.modern_name: H^1 realization of motives of abelian type; h^1(X) ↔ Pic^0/Alb
ideas.where_published: Kleiman 1968 (Dix exposés) treats the degree-1 case of the standard conjectures along these lines

ideas.what: An algebraic correspondence acting on H^1 of abelian varieties comes from a homomorphism (Lemma 1.7 used here)
ideas.modern_name: Hom(B,A)⊗Z_ℓ ↪ Hom(T_ℓB,T_ℓA) and full faithfulness of h^1 on abelian varieties for algebraic classes
ideas.usually_credited_to: Weil; Tate for the full Galois version (1966)

ideas.what: The induced homomorphism depends only on the numerical equivalence class of the correspondence
ideas.modern_name: num = hom for the H^1-part / Weil trace-form nondegeneracy

deep.surprise_reason: A careful but classical step: the Picard–Albanese homomorphism induced by a 1-cycle correspondence is identified with its ℓ-adic H^1 action. This belongs to the degree-1 part of the standard-conjecture programme, which Kleiman and Lieberman published around 1968. Nothing here goes beyond the known record.
transcription_corrections: 'l premier à la car. t'istiques [?]' should read 'l premier à la caractéristique'.
The superscript in a(γ^{[-m-n-1]}(ξ)) is garbled. The intended class is that of a codimension n+m-1 cycle, so read a(γ^{n+m-1}(ξ)) or simply a(γ(ξ)).
'classe d'équivalence numérique de ξ Z' most likely means 'de Z'; the ξ is stray.
In 'Considérons l'homomorphisme composé ψ_X a(γ(ξ)) φ_X^{(1)}' the manuscript indeed has φ_X^{(1)}, but this is Grothendieck's slip for (φ_Y^{(1)})^{-1}.
The demonstration's crossed-out word 'équivalence' before 'correspondances algébriques' is correctly marked as deleted.
